Who founded Justice and Development Party (Turkey)?

Merlin: Ron Moody. Geoffrey's account presented Merlin as a prophet and royal advisor to Arthur's father, Uther Pendragon.

Saint Valentine's Day Massacre: United States. The Saint Valentine's Day Massacre was the murder of seven members and associates of Chicago's North Side Gang on Saint Valentine's Day 1929.
In which country is Battle of Crete?
Battle of Crete: Greece. It began on the morning of 20 May 1941, with multiple German airborne landings on Crete.

Second Spanish Republic: Spain. The Republic was proclaimed on 14 April 1931 after the deposition of King Alfonso XIII.

In which country did the Battle of Crécy take place?
Battle of Crécy: France. The Battle of Crécy took place on 26 August 1346 in northern France between a French army commanded by King Philip VI and an English army led by King Edward III.
Transylvania: Romania. The region's natural border to the east and south is the Carpathian Mountains, and to the west it is the Apuseni Mountains.
In which country did the Battle of Fontenoy take place?
Battle of Fontenoy: Belgium. The Battle of Fontenoy, 11 May 1745, took place during the War of the Austrian Succession, near Tournai, in Belgium.
In which country was the Duchy of Brittany?
Duchy of Brittany: Kingdom of France. The Duchy of Brittany was a medieval feudal state that existed between approximately 939 and 1547.
Which of these was an official language of Mercia?
Mercia: Old English. Mercia was an early medieval English kingdom, one of the seven kingdoms of the Anglo-Saxon period.
Which of these was an official language of the Empire of Trebizond?
Empire of Trebizond: Greek. The empire consisted of the Pontus, or far northeastern corner of Anatolia, and portions of southern Crimea.
Which of these was an official language of Regency of Algiers?
Regency of Algiers: Ottoman Turkish. The Regency of Algiers was an early modern semi-independent Ottoman province and nominal vassal state on the Barbary Coast of North Africa from 1516 to 1830.
Which of these was an official language of the Seleucid Empire?
Seleucid Empire: Ancient Greek. The Seleucid Empire ( sih-LEW-sid) was a Greek state in West Asia during the Hellenistic period.
Trained as a pediatrician in Egypt, this Palestinian leader co-founded a major militant political movement in 1987 and led its council for a matter of weeks in 2004. Who is he?
Abdel Aziz al-Rantisi (23 October 1947 - 17 April 2004) was a Palestinian political leader and co-founder of Hamas, along with Sheikh Ahmed Yassin in 1987.

This German officer rose to the rank of field marshal in the Luftwaffe during World War II, becoming one of Nazi Germany's most highly decorated commanders after a career spanning both world wars — who was he?
Albert Kesselring (30 November 1885 - 15 July 1960) was a German military officer who served in the Luftwaffe during World War II.

A War Democrat who ran on Lincoln's National Union ticket, he took the presidency after the assassination — then clashed so bitterly with Congress over Reconstruction that the House impeached him. Which 17th president was it?
Andrew Johnson (December 29, 1808 - July 31, 1875) was the 17th president of the United States, serving from 1865 to 1869.
A former communist who championed privatization, this president led a relatively less-authoritarian Central Asian state until the 2005 Tulip Revolution swept him out — who was he?
Askar Akayev (born 10 November 1944) is a Kyrgyz former politician who served as President of Kyrgyzstan from 1990 until being overthrown in the March 2005 Tulip Revolution.
Known colloquially as PNoy, this 15th president of the Philippines was the son of an assassinated senator and the 11th president — who was he?
Benigno Aquino III (locally; February 8, 1960 - June 24, 2021), also known colloquially as PNoy, was the 15th president of the Philippines, serving from 2010 to 2016.
This Persian King of Kings died from a gangrenous thigh wound while marching home to crush a revolt, having earlier added Egypt and Cyrenaica to his empire — who was he?
Cambyses II was the second King of Kings of the Achaemenid Empire, reigning from 530 to 522 BCE.
She served as Canada's deputy prime minister from 2019 to 2024 after negotiating a major North American trade deal as foreign affairs minister — who is she?
Chrystia Freeland (born August 2, 1968) is a Canadian politician and journalist who served as the tenth deputy prime minister of Canada from 2019 to 2024.

Iceland's longest-serving prime minister, this former mayor of Reykjavík later chaired the Central Bank — only to face loud public demands for his resignation amid the 2008 financial crisis. Who was he?
Davíð Oddsson (17 January 1948 - 1 March 2026) was an Icelandic politician, and the longest-serving prime minister of Iceland, in office from 1991 to 2004.
Once director of his country's military academy, this Guatemalan officer seized power in 1982 for a brief, blood-soaked tenure that later brought accusations of genocide — who was he?
Efraín Ríos Montt (16 June 1926 - 1 April 2018) was a Guatemalan military officer who served as de facto President of Guatemala from 1982 to 1983.
Headquartered in Deventer, Overijssel, and currently led by Henk Vermeer, this agrarian right-wing populist Dutch political party champions rural interests — which party?
Farmer–Citizen Movement (BBB) is an agrarian and right-wing populist political party in the Netherlands.
Before becoming governor of California, this Democrat was mayor of San Francisco and founded the PlumpJack winery with Gordon Getty as an investor. Who is he?
Gavin Newsom (born October 10, 1967) is an American politician and businessman serving as the governor of California since 2019.
This Ecuadorian banker and businessman served as his country's 47th president from 2021 to 2023, having earlier been Superminister of Economy and Governor of Guayas province — who is he?
Guillermo Lasso (Latin American; born 16 November 1955) is an Ecuadorian businessman, banker and politician who served as the 47th president of Ecuador from 2021 to 2023.
Historians now question this traditional label for early medieval England's patchwork of seven petty kingdoms, since the number of realms actually fluctuated over time — what's the term?

Heptarchy was the division of Anglo-Saxon England between the sixth and eighth centuries into petty kingdoms, conventionally the seven kingdoms of East Anglia, Essex, Kent, Mercia, Northumbria, Sussex, and Wessex.

This French historian of Russia served as Perpetual Secretary of the Académie Française from 1999 until her death in 2023, having earlier sat in the European Parliament for the Gaullist RPR party — who is she?
Hélène Carrère d'Encausse (French; ne Zourabichvili; 6 July 1929 - 5 August 2023) was a French political historian who specialised in Russian history.

This Indian religion teaches spiritual purity through strict nonviolence toward all living creatures, guided by 24 supreme teachers called tirthankaras who have conquered the cycle of rebirth — name the religion?
Jainism is an Indian religion that teaches a path toward spiritual purity and enlightenment through disciplined nonviolence (ahimsa) to all living creatures.

John Dean (born October 14, 1938) is a disbarred American attorney who served as White House Counsel for U.S.
Before becoming Tunisia's head of state in 2019, this jurist led the country's Association of Constitutional Law for over two decades — who is he?
Kais Saied (born 22 February 1958) is a Tunisian politician, jurist and former assistant professor of law who has served as the fifth president of Tunisia since 2019.

Started by a trader named Arndt who joined a merchants' guild in Essen, this 400-year-old dynasty later founded a cast-steel works during the Napoleonic Wars and armed the German Empire — which family?
Krupp family is a prominent 400-year-old German dynasty from Essen, noted for its production of steel, artillery, ammunition and other armaments.

This Germanic people migrated south from near present-day Hamburg, eventually conquering most of the Italian Peninsula in the late 6th century — a northern Italian region still bears their name — who were they?
Lombards were a Germanic people who conquered most of the Italian Peninsula between 568 and 774 AD.

Convicted in 2018 of acting as an unregistered foreign agent within the United States, this Russian political activist and journalist had previously worked as an assistant to a senior United Russia party figure. Who is she?

Maria Butina (born 10 November 1988) is a Russian politician, political activist, journalist, and former entrepreneur who was convicted in 2018 of acting as an unregistered foreign agent of Russia within the United States.
Born in Brookline to Greek immigrant parents, this Massachusetts governor became the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 1988 — who is he?
Michael Dukakis (duu-; born November 3, 1933) is an American politician and lawyer who was governor of Massachusetts from 1975 to 1979 and from 1983 to 1991.
Ruling as head of his country's royal family since 1986, this king holds executive authority over government and is constitutionally immune from prosecution — who is he?
Mswati III (born Makhosetive Dlamini; 19 April 1968) is the Ngwenyama (King) of Eswatini and head of the Swazi royal family since 1986.
Having sat on France's Constitutional Council since 2013, this jurist later led the Justice Ministry under Édouard Philippe and Education under Gabriel Attal — who is she?
Nicole Belloubet (born 15 June 1955) is a French jurist and politician who served as Minister of National Education in the government of Prime Minister Gabriel Attal in 2024.
The first prime minister of India from the south of the country, this Indian National Congress statesman is credited with launching India's economic liberalization after the 1991 crisis — who is he?

P. V. Narasimha Rao (28 June 1921 - 23 December 2004) was an Indian independence activist, lawyer, and statesman from the Indian National Congress who served as the prime minister of India from 1991 to 1996.

Reigning nearly 32 years, the longest verified papacy after Saint Peter, this 19th-century pontiff convoked the First Vatican Council in 1868, which defined papal infallibility before adjourning for good in 1870 — who was he?

Pope Pius IX (born Giovanni Maria Battista Pietro Pellegrino Isidoro Mastai-Ferretti; 13 May 1792 - 7 February 1878) was head of the Catholic Church from 16 June 1846 until his death in February 1878.
This French president co-founded the Democratic Republican Alliance in 1902 and visited Russia in 1912 and 1914 to mend ties strained by earlier crises — who is he?
Raymond Poincaré (20 August 1860 - 15 October 1934) was a French statesman who served as President of France from 1913 to 1920, and three times as Prime Minister of France.
Fought in 1904–05 over rival ambitions in Manchuria and Korea, this war's great clashes raged near Mukden on land and across the Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan — what was it?
Russo-Japanese War (8 February 1904 - 5 September 1905) was fought between the Russian Empire and the Empire of Japan over rival imperial ambitions in Manchuria and the Korean Empire.
Lord of the desert and the balancing counterpart to Horus, which ancient Egyptian god of storms and chaos murdered his own brother Osiris?
Set (deity) is a god of deserts, storms, disorder, violence, and foreigners in ancient Egyptian religion.
He co-founded the modern Conservative Party of Canada and served as its very first leader before becoming the country's 22nd prime minister in 2006 — who is this Calgary-trained economist?
Stephen Harper (born April 30, 1959) is a Canadian politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Canada from 2006 to 2015.
This Flavian emperor became the first Roman ruler ever to succeed his own biological father, having earlier made his name besieging Jerusalem in the Jewish revolt — who was he?
Titus (30 December 39 - 13 September 81 AD) was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD.
This Hungarian lawyer first became prime minister in 1998, leading his country into NATO, then returned to power in 2010 atop the party Fidesz — who is it?
Viktor Orbán (born 31 May 1963) is a Hungarian lawyer and politician who served as the prime minister of Hungary from 1998 to 2002 and from 2010 to 2026.

Called the "father of modern Liberia," this man pursued a policy of national unification to narrow the gap between Americo-Liberians and indigenous Liberians during a long presidency that ended only at his death in 1971. Who was he?
William Tubman (29 November 1895 - 23 July 1971) was a Liberian politician.

Renowned as a criminal defense lawyer for his string of acquittals — which earned him a nickname referencing that very skill — this outspoken French-Italian attorney went on to serve as Minister of Justice from 2020 to 2024. Who is he?

Éric Dupond-Moretti (born 20 April 1961) is a French-Italian lawyer and politician who served as Minister of Justice from 2020 to 2024 in the successive governments of Prime Ministers Jean Castex, lisabeth Borne and Gabriel Attal.
This Austrian-born politician became chancellor of Germany in 1933 and took the title Führer the next year, launching the Second World War with his 1939 invasion of Poland — who was he?
Adolf Hitler: Dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945.
This Athenian general switched sides repeatedly during the Peloponnesian War — advising Sparta after fleeing sacrilege charges at home, then defecting again to advise a Persian satrap — who was he?
Alcibiades: Athenian general and statesman (c. 450–404 BC)

Fought 1861-1865 between a northern union and a southern confederacy formed to preserve slavery, this US conflict ended in union victory and the abolition of slavery, freeing four million people — which war?
American Civil War: 1861–1865 conflict in the United States.
Holding the New South Wales seat of Grayndler since 1996, this economics graduate became Australia's 31st prime minister in 2022 — who is it?
Anthony Albanese: Prime Minister of Australia since 2022. Anthony Norman Albanese (born 2 March 1963) is an Australian politician who has served as the 31st prime minister of Australia since 2022.

Worshipped from the Bronze Age onward, this Hellenized Near Eastern goddess was the Semitic counterpart to Ishtar and was carried by Phoenician traders all the way to their colonies on the Iberian Peninsula — who is she?
Astarte: Middle Eastern goddess, worshipped from the Bronze Age through classical antiquity.
In 53 BC, seven Roman legions under Crassus were lured into the desert and crushed by Parthian cataphracts and horse archers near a town in modern-day Turkey — what was this military clash called?
Battle of Carrhae: Part of the Roman–Parthian Wars.

"Keeper of greatness" was the meaning of his name — fitting for the 13th and final emperor of Vietnam's Nguyễn dynasty, who abdicated in August 1945 after Japan surrendered. Who was he?
Bảo Đại: Last emperor of Vietnam from 1926 to 1945 (1913–1997)

Chaco War: War between Bolivia and Paraguay (1932 to 1935). The Chaco War (Spanish: Guerra del Chaco, Guarani: Cháko Ñorairõ) was fought from 1932 to 1935.
This Imperial Japanese Navy admiral led the carrier strike force that attacked Pearl Harbor in 1941, then suffered a crushing defeat at Midway the following year — who is he?

Cuban Revolution: 1955–1958 sociopolitical change in Cuba.

Democracy: Government system where political power lies with the people.
The eldest of a hundred brothers born to King Dhritarashtra, this Mahabharata antagonist humiliated Draupadi in a rigged dice game, provoking Bhima's vow of revenge — who is he?
Duryodhana: Eldest Kaurava in the epic Mahabharata.
The longest-serving U.S. first lady, she went on to help draft the Universal Declaration of Human Rights as a UN delegate, earning a standing ovation when it was adopted — who was she?
Eleanor Roosevelt: American diplomat and activist (1884–1962)
A five-time Socialist Party candidate for U.S. president, this labor leader co-founded the Industrial Workers of the World and led a major railway strike against the CB&Q line in 1888. Who is he?
Eugene V. Debs: American labor and political leader (1855–1926)
It erupted in 1989 when Charles Taylor's NPFL invaded from Ivory Coast to topple President Samuel Doe, who was soon captured and executed by a splinter faction — which conflict is this?
First Liberian Civil War: 1989–1997 war in West Africa.
Dwelling in the wetland halls of Fensalir, this Norse goddess of marriage and prophecy was the wife of Odin — who is she?
Frigg: Germanic goddess. The names ultimately stem from the Proto-Germanic theonym *Frijjō.
Codenamed Operation Marita, this April 1941 World War II assault followed Italy's failed 1940 attack and culminated in airborne landings on Crete — which campaign is it?

German invasion of Greece: World War II military campaign in 1941. The German invasion of Greece or Operation Marita (German: Unternehmen Marita), were the attacks on Greece by Italy and Germany during World War II.
A protégé of Arnulfo Arias who became the leading opponent of the Noriega dictatorship, this lawyer served as president of Panama from 1989 to 1994 — who is he?

Guillermo Endara: President of Panama from 1989 to 1994. Guillermo David Endara Galimany (May 12, 1936 – September 28, 2009) was a Panamanian politician who served as the president of Panama from 1989 to 1994.
Often seen as a personification of storm winds, which half-human, half-bird creature from Greek and Roman mythology appears in Homer's poems?
Harpy: Half-bird half-woman monsters associated with storm winds.
Ruling Galilee and Perea as tetrarch, this New Testament figure is blamed for the executions of John the Baptist and Jesus of Nazareth — who was he?
Herod Antipas: 1st-century AD tetrarch of Galilee and Perea (r. 1–39)
Leading Bavaria's Free Voters party since 2018, this politician also serves as the state's deputy minister president and economics minister — who is he?
Born in 1923 at a police congress in Vienna, this Lyon-based body is the world's largest international police organization, with a National Central Bureau in all 196 member states — what is it?
Interpol: International police organization. It is headquartered in Lyon, France, with seven regional bureaus worldwide, and a National Central Bureau in all 196 member states.
Born in December 2014, this heir apparent to the Monegasque throne — twin brother of Princess Gabriella and son of Albert II and Charlene — has held the title Marquis of Baux since birth. Who is he?

Jacques, Hereditary Prince of Monaco: Heir apparent to the Monégasque throne (born 2014). Jacques, Hereditary Prince of Monaco, Marquis of Baux (Jacques Honoré Rainier Grimaldi; born 10 December 2014), is the heir apparent to the Monegasque throne.
After nearly going bankrupt as an MP, this English novelist bounced back with the blockbuster Kane and Abel, later becoming a Conservative life peer — who is he?
Jeffrey Archer: English author and politician (born 1940)

Dubbed the 'Father of the American Navy,' this Scottish-born officer fled to Virginia after killing a mutinous subordinate before leading naval raids on British shipping in the Irish and North Seas — who is he?
John Paul Jones: Scottish-born naval officer (1747–1792)

Louis Philippe I styled himself 'King of the French' rather than 'King of France' during this liberal regime that began with an 1830 revolution and ended with another uprising in 1848 — what was it called?
Son of Khufu, this Fourth Dynasty king built the second-largest pyramid at Giza and, some egyptologists say, the Great Sphinx itself. Who was he?
Khafre: Ancient Egyptian pharaoh of 4th dynasty.
In Śaiva Tantra, what is the name for the divine feminine energy said to coil at the base of the spine, whose awakening through meditation is believed to lead to liberation?
Kundalini: Form of divine energy in Hindu mysticism.
A slave owner and leading champion of 'popular sovereignty,' he served in the cabinets of Andrew Jackson and James Buchanan and was the 1848 Democratic presidential nominee — who is he?
Lewis Cass: United States Army officer and politician (1782–1866)

This Colombian liberal politician and journalist, who founded the New Liberalism movement and declared himself an enemy of the drug cartels, was assassinated in 1989 before the presidential vote — who was he?

Luis Carlos Galán: Colombian politician (1943–1989). While the investigation into his assassination remains unsolved, Galan's assassination was a crucial factor in the downfall of the Medellin Cartel a few years later.
Sanskrit for 'circle,' this geometric configuration of symbols is used across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Shinto traditions to aid meditation and represent sacred space — what is it?
Mandala: Spiritual and ritual symbol in Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism.
Famed for slicing his military cloak in two with his sword to clothe a freezing beggar, this Roman-cavalry-veteran-turned-bishop became one of Europe's most venerated patron saints — who was he?
Martin of Tours: Christian cleric and saint (316/336–397)
Originating in Judaism, this Hebrew term for an anointed savior figure describes a future human leader descended from King David who will reunite the tribes of Israel — what is the title?
Messiah: Saviour or liberator of a group of people.
Killed during Hernán Cortés's seizure of Tenochtitlan, this ninth Aztec emperor presided over the empire at its largest territorial extent — who was he?
Moctezuma II: Tlahtoāni of the Aztec Empire until 1520.
Son of Mehmed III and Halime Sultan, this Ottoman ruler held the throne twice, briefly in 1617–1618 and again in 1622–1623 — who was he?
Mustafa I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (r. 1617–1618, 1622–1623)
On the eve of WWII, this British stockbroker quietly arranged the rescue of 669 mostly-Jewish children from Czechoslovakia, finding them homes and sponsors in Britain — who was he?
Nicholas Winton: British banker and humanitarian (1909–2015)
This retired Marine lieutenant colonel and Vietnam veteran devised the plan to divert Iran arms-sale profits to Contra rebels, testifying before Congress under limited immunity — who is he?

In 1925, this British physicist became the first to prove that radioactivity could transmute one chemical element into another, later winning a Nobel Prize and pioneering operational research for the Allied war effort — who is he?
Serving as Vietnam's eighth prime minister from 2021 to 2026, this former lieutenant general once led the Communist Party's organizing commission — who is he?

Phạm Minh Chính: Prime Minister of Vietnam from 2021 to 2026. Phạm Minh Chính (Vietnamese: [faːm˧˨ʔ mïŋ˧˧ t͡ɕïŋ˧˦]; born 10 December 1958) is a Vietnamese politician and former public security lieutenant general.
Nicknamed the 'Black Baron,' this scion of a Baltic German noble family became the last commander-in-chief of the White forces in southern Russia during the Civil War — who was he?

Modeled on a notorious wave of Revolutionary France violence, this campaign of political repression and mass executions was carried out by the Bolshevik secret police during the Russian Civil War — what is it called?
Red Terror: Bolshevik campaign of political repression and executions (1918–1922)
The first Philippine president from Mindanao and the oldest to take office at 71, this former Davao City mayor led the country from 2016 — who is it?
Rodrigo Duterte: President of the Philippines from 2016 to 2022.
Born Rozbih Khwushbudhan and trained as a Zoroastrian magus, this companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad converted to Islam after meeting him in Medina — who was he?

Salman the Persian: Companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. Muhammad specifically said "Salman is part of my Ahl al-Bayt." In meetings with the other companions, he was often referred to by the kunya Abu ʿAbdullah.

Touched off by the staged 1931 Mukden incident and the puppet state of Manchukuo, this 1937–1945 conflict — China's largest war of the 20th century — is often called the start of World War II in Asia. What was it?
Second Sino-Japanese War: 1937–1945 conflict in East Asia. It is often regarded as the beginning of World War II in Asia, as the wars became heavily intertwined after Japan's entry into World War II.

Known as 'The Destroyer' within the Hindu trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu, this deity is the Supreme Lord who creates, protects, and transforms the universe in one major tradition. Who is this god?
Shiva: Major deity in Hinduism. Shiva is one of the five equivalent deities in Panchayatana puja of the Smarta tradition of Hinduism.
A Thracian gladiator born near the Strymon river, this figure led an escaped-slave uprising against the Roman Republic known as the Third Servile War — who was he?
Spartacus: Thracian gladiator who led a slave revolt. Spartacus is described to be born near the Strymon river, in Thrace (now known as Bulgaria), possibly from the Maedi tribe.
Sparked by Arab Spring protests against Bashar al-Assad in March 2011, this nearly 14-year conflict ended with the regime's fall in December 2024 — what is it?
Syrian civil war: 2011–2024 armed conflict in Syria.

Ruling the Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy from 493 to 526 and later regent of the Visigoths too, this king received the old Western imperial regalia from Constantinople and was addressed by Italy's aristocracy as princeps. Who was he?
Theodoric the Great: King of Italy from 493 to 526. As ruler of the combined Gothic realms, Theodoric controlled an empire stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to the Adriatic Sea.
Hailed by the Senate as "the best ruler" and counted among the Five Good Emperors, this Hispania-born soldier pushed Rome to its greatest-ever territorial extent. Which emperor?
Trajan: Roman emperor from AD 98 to 117.
Born in Jaffna, this guerrilla leader founded and led a militant organization in a decades-long campaign for an independent Tamil state in Sri Lanka — who is he?
Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine
Velupillai Prabhakaran: Leader of militant Tamil organisation in Sri Lanka (1954–2009)
This Chinese diplomat served as ambassador to Japan before becoming Minister of Foreign Affairs and later director of the Communist Party's Central Foreign Affairs Commission Office — who is he?
Alongside Andrew Moray, this Scottish knight won the Battle of Stirling Bridge in 1297 before being captured and executed for treason in 1305 — who is he?
William Wallace: Scottish knight (1270–1305). Along with Andrew Moray, Wallace defeated an English army at the Battle of Stirling Bridge in September 1297.

Born to a family of strawberry farmers in Akita Prefecture, this politician rose to become Japan's Prime Minister from 2020 to 2021 after years as Chief Cabinet Secretary under Shinzo Abe — who is he?

Yoshihide Suga: Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021. Yoshihide Suga (菅 義偉, Suga Yoshihide; born 6 December 1948) is a Japanese former politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 2020 to 2021.

Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four has been around longest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
James Franck is a physicist. Franck became the head of the physics division of the Kaiser Wilhelm Gesellschaft for Physical Chemistry.
Who among these is a chemist?
Linus Pauling is a chemist. Linus Carl Pauling ( PAW-ling; February 28, 1901 – August 19, 1994) was an American chemist and peace activist.
What is the atomic number of Lawrencium?
Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lr (formerly Lw) and atomic number 103.
In what year was Dolph Lundgren born?
Dolph Lundgren: Hans "Dolph" Lundgren (Swedish: [ˈdɔlːf ˈlɵ̌nːdɡreːn]; born 3 November 1957) is a Swedish-American actor, filmmaker, and martial artist.
In what year was Molybdenum discovered?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
In what year was Titanium discovered?
Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
Mikoyan MiG-27: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. It is based on the Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 fighter aircraft, but optimised for air-to-ground attack.
Which country is Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider from?

Northrop Grumman B-21 Raider: United States. Part of the Long Range Strike Bomber (LRS-B) program, it is to be an intercontinental strategic bomber that can deliver conventional and thermonuclear weapons.
Who is credited with discovering Indium?
Indium: Ferdinand Reich. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Who is credited with discovering Californium?
Californium: Stanley Gerald Thompson. Californium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cf and atomic number 98.
Who is credited with discovering Fluorine?
Fluorine: Henri Moissan. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
This is the most common genetic cause of dwarfism, typically producing short arms and legs with a normal-length torso and an enlarged head with a prominent forehead — what condition is it?
Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder whose primary feature is dwarfism.
Often caused by misaligned or unevenly focused eyes in early childhood, this is the most common cause of single-eye vision loss in kids and young adults, nicknamed 'lazy eye' — what condition is it?
Amblyopia is a disorder of sight in which the brain fails to fully process input from one eye and over time favors the other eye.
A physician who called medicine his lawful wife and literature his mistress, this Russian writer produced four stage classics and ranks among modernism's founders — who is he?
Anton Chekhov was Russian dramatist and author (1860–1904).
Which genus of early hominins, which lived in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, gave rise to the genera Homo, Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus?
Australopithecus (-loh-; or, os-, from Latin australis southern 'grc' and (pthkos) ape) is a genus of early hominins that existed in Africa during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene.
This red-orange compound, formed from the breakdown of heme, is further processed into pigments that give feces their brown color and urine its straw-yellow hue. What is it?
Bilirubin (BR) (adopted from German, originally bili, for bile, plus ruber, Latin for red) is a red-orange compound that occurs as the reduction product of biliverdin, a breakdown product of heme.

Named for its bread-like texture and potato-like flavor when cooked, this tropical tree fruit spread through Oceania via ancient seafaring migrations before European navigators brought Polynesian varieties to the Caribbean — which fruit?
Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) is a species of flowering tree in the mulberry and jackfruit family (Moraceae).
Discovered in 1940, this non-intoxicating compound extracted from cannabis is used medically as an anticonvulsant for two rare, severe forms of childhood epilepsy — what is it?
Cannabidiol (CBD) is a phytocannabinoid, one of 113 identified cannabinoids in Cannabis, along with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), and accounts for up to 40% of the plant's extract.

The scientific study of matter's properties and behavior, this physical science occupies an intermediate position between physics and biology, sometimes called the central science. What is this field of study?
Chemistry is the scientific study of the properties and behavior of matter. Chemistry also addresses the nature of chemical bonds in chemical compounds.
Domed-backed little beetles that mostly hunt aphids, they wear aposematic spots to warn off predators and are named for 'lady' Mary — what's the scientific family?
Coccinellidae is a widespread family of small beetles.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.

Distinguished from their one-leaved cousins by a pair of embryonic seed leaves, this classic angiosperm classification was shown by molecular science not to form a single evolutionary lineage — which plant group?
Dicotyledon (or, more rarely, dicotyls), are one of the two groups into which all the flowering plants (angiosperms) were formerly divided.
Born in North Carolina in 1983, this former NSA contractor leaked classified files exposing global surveillance programs after working for the CIA, Dell, and a defense contractor — name him?

Edward Snowden (born June 21, 1983) is a former United States National Security Agency (NSA) intelligence contractor who leaked classified documents revealing the existence of global surveillance programs.
Also called grain alcohol, this volatile compound with the formula C2H5OH is the active ingredient in every alcoholic beverage — what is it?
Ethanol (also called ethyl alcohol, grain alcohol, drinking alcohol, or simply alcohol) is an organic compound with the chemical formula CH3CH2OH.
This everyday bodily process — expelling gas from the intestines through the anus — has its own dedicated field of scientific study named after it: what's the term for the process itself?
Flatulence is the expulsion of gas from the intestines via the anus, commonly referred to as farting.
Ordained a priest in 1923, this Belgian physicist connected an expanding universe to Einstein's field equations and floated an early Big Bang hypothesis — who was he?
Georges Lemaître (lə-MET-rə; 17 July 1894 - 20 June 1966) was a Belgian Catholic priest, theoretical physicist, and mathematician who made major contributions to cosmology and astrophysics.
Born Herman Webster Mudgett, this con artist and killer worked his crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition, earning the nickname "the Beast of Chicago" — who was he?
H. H. Holmes (May 16, 1861 - May 7, 1896), better known as Dr.

Often called the "father of the Indian nuclear programme," this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and the research centre later renamed in his honour. Who was he?
Homi J. Bhabha (30 October 1909 - 24 January 1966) was an Indian nuclear theoretical physicist who is widely credited as the "father of the Indian nuclear programme".

Dubbed the 'saviour of mothers,' this 19th-century Hungarian doctor demonstrated that a simple hygiene practice could drastically cut deaths from childbed fever, decades before germ theory was widely accepted — who is he?

Ignaz Semmelweis (1 July 1818 - 13 August 1865) was a Hungarian medical doctor and scientist of German descent who was an early pioneer of antiseptic procedures and was described as the "saviour of mothers".
Most of the flowers used by the global perfume industry for this fragrant genus of shrubs and vines are grown in a single Egyptian village. What plant is it?
Jasmine (botanical name: Jasminum) is a genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family of Oleaceae.
Diagnosed via corneal topography and linked to frequent eye rubbing and allergies, this progressive disorder causes the cornea to bulge into a cone shape — which eye condition?
Keratoconus is an eye disorder in which the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye, gradually thins and bulges outward into a cone shape.
Caused by Mycobacterium bacteria, this ancient nerve-damaging disease can dull a person's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed wounds cost them their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy (HD), is a long-term infection by the bacterium Mycobacterium leprae or Mycobacterium lepromatosis.
Born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families, this philosopher studied under Bertrand Russell at Cambridge and transformed 20th-century philosophy of language and logic — who is he?

Ludwig Wittgenstein ((h)tyne; Austrian; 26 April 1889 - 29 April 1951) was an Austro-British philosopher who worked in logic, philosophy of mathematics, philosophy of mind, and philosophy of language.

In 1835 she and Caroline Herschel became the first female Honorary Members of the Royal Astronomical Society, and decades later this Scottish polymath's name topped John Stuart Mill's women's-suffrage petition. Who is she?
Mary Somerville (ne Fairfax, formerly Greig; 1780-1872) was a Scottish scientist, writer, and polymath.
Entering Soviet service in 1983 alongside the larger Su-27, this 'Fulcrum' air-superiority fighter was later adapted into a multirole jet — which aircraft is it?
Mikoyan MiG-29 (NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
When the radial fibres of the iris over-dilate the pupil beyond its normal light response, what do doctors call this condition?
Mydriasis is the dilation of the pupil, usually having a non-physiological cause, or sometimes a physiological pupillary response.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and the most common cause of gastroenteritis, this fecal–orally spread bug usually strikes about 24 hours after exposure. What is it?
Norovirus is the most common cause of gastroenteritis. Norovirus, also known as Norwalk virus, is the most common cause of gastroenteritis.
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compounds pairs oxygen with at least one other element — even the thin protective skin on aluminum foil counts as one — what's the class?
Oxide is a chemical compound containing at least one oxygen atom and one other element in its chemical formula.
Named from Greek words for 'odd' and 'toe,' this mammalian order groups horses, rhinoceroses, and tapirs together based on their toe count. Which order?
Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek, perisss 'odd' and, dktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.

This common skin condition begins with a single scaly 'herald patch,' followed weeks later by an eruption of smaller pinkish spots, and typically clears on its own within three months. What is it called?
Pityriasis rosea is a type of skin rash.
Roaming the interior of western and central North America, this even-toed mammal survived the Pleistocene extinction of its close relatives and evolved to resemble an antelope — which creature is it?
Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.

Distinguished from their smaller rodent cousins mainly by size, these long-tailed rodents span dozens of genera worldwide, with Rattus being the most familiar — of the 56 known species, what are they collectively called?
Rat are various medium-sized, long-tailed rodents.

Originally bred in Germany to herd livestock and pull carts of butchered meat to market until railways took over in the mid-1800s, this medium-to-large mastiff-type dog now also works as a guard and police dog - name the breed?
Rottweiler (UK also) is a breed of domestic mastiff type dog, regarded as medium-to-large or large.
Made by Novo Nordisk and taken by injection or pill, this peptide medicine doubles as a diabetes treatment and a weight-management drug — what is it?
Semaglutide is an anti-diabetic medication used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes, and an anti-obesity medication used for weight management.

With the formula NaNO3 and historically mined in massive deposits in Chile, this white, deliquescent salt is a key industrial source used to make fertilizers, pyrotechnics, and explosives — which compound?
Sodium nitrate is the chemical compound with the formula NaNO3. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.

Tracing its lineage back to ancestral fish from the Early Jurassic period roughly 174 to 201 million years ago, this family of 27 fish species is one of only two living branches of an ancient order that also includes the paddlefish — name this fish family?
Sturgeon are the 27 species of fish belonging to the family Acipenseridae.

Named for the order of fish that includes pufferfish, this potent neurotoxin also turns up in blue-ringed octopuses and rough-skinned newts, and is actually produced by symbiotic bacteria rather than the animals themselves — what's the toxin?

Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is a potent neurotoxin. Its name derives from Tetraodontiformes, an order that includes pufferfish, porcupinefish, ocean sunfish, and triggerfish; several of these species carry the toxin.
Not a single branch of the family of life but a strategy evolved over and over — a tall trunk and branches reaching for sunlight — describes which kind of perennial plant?
Tree is a perennial plant with an elongated stem, or trunk, usually supporting branches and leaves.

This flowering plant genus, the largest in its family with over 680 species, is found mostly across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but also as far-flung as Hawaii and the Andes. What is this plant commonly called?
Viola (plant) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Violaceae.
This mosquito-borne viral disease causes chills, nausea, and muscle pain, and in about 15% of cases progresses to liver damage that turns the skin a telltale color — what disease is it?
Yellow fever is a viral disease of typically short duration.
Caused by excess growth hormone after the body's growth plates have closed, this disorder first shows up as enlarged hands and feet before affecting the jaw and forehead — what condition is it?
Acromegaly: Human disease that results in excess growth of certain parts of the body.
Also called the Persian silk tree or mimosa tree, this flowering species in the pea family is native to Asia — what is it?

Albizia julibrissin: Species of plant. Albizia julibrissin, the Persian silk tree, pink silk tree, or mimosa tree, is a species of tree in the Fabaceae family, native to southwestern and eastern Asia.
This functional group, formed by replacing a carboxylic acid's hydroxyl with an amino group, creates the peptide bonds that link amino acids into proteins — what is it?
Amide: Organic compounds of the form RC(=O)NR′R″.

A German pharmacist coined this pigment's name from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue' in 1835 — it shifts red to purple to blue depending on pH and colors blueberries, black rice, and autumn leaves; what is it?
A notoriously toxic metalloid and pnictogen with atomic number 33, it's used in lead alloys for car batteries and ammunition and as a semiconductor dopant — which element is it?
Arsenic: Chemical element with atomic number 33 (As). It is a metalloid and one of the pnictogens, and therefore shares many properties with its group 15 neighbors phosphorus and antimony.
The world's largest nocturnal primate, this Madagascar lemur has ever-growing rodent-like teeth and taps tree trunks with a bony middle finger to fish out grubs by echo — which animal?
Aye-aye: Species of primate. This foraging method is called percussive foraging, and takes up 5–41% of the aye-aye's foraging time.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
This North American wild cat earns its name from the black-tipped, stubby tail it sports, along with distinctive black bars on its forelegs — one of the four species of lynx. Which animal is it?
Bobcat: Medium-sized North American wild cat.

Best known for his role as Ben Hunter in a soapy prime-time revenge drama, this American actor also starred as Will Davis on The CW's 'Privileged' and Kyle Parks on Lifetime's 'The Client List.' Who is he?
Formed when quicklime reacts with water, this compound goes by names like slaked lime and builders' lime, and is used in food prep under the additive code E526 — what is it?
Calcium hydroxide: Inorganic compound of formula Ca(OH)2.

This American Nobel laureate coined the term 'bioorthogonal chemistry' for reactions that work inside living systems, building chemical tools to study the cell-surface sugars called glycans. Who is she?
Despite no clinical evidence it treats any disease, this daisy-like herb is brewed into calming teas and can trigger uterine contractions in its Roman variety — what is it?
Chamomile: Common name for several daisy-like plants.
Named after a 17th-century English physician, this ring-shaped network of arteries supplies blood to the brain in humans and other vertebrates — what is it called?
Circle of Willis: Circulatory anastomosis that supplies blood to the brain and surrounding structures.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Smelling of vanilla but tasting bitter, which plant compound isn't itself an anticoagulant, though its derivatives inspired the blood-thinning drug warfarin?
This Zambian-born economist turned heads with four New York Times bestsellers, including "Dead Aid," which argues that foreign aid actually holds Africa back. Which author and life peer is it?
Dambisa Moyo, Baroness Moyo: Zambian-born economist (born February 1969)
Known for feigning death when cornered, which genus of cat-sized marsupials includes the only marsupial species found north of Mexico?
Didelphis: Genus of marsupials. The six species in the genus Didelphis, commonly known as Large American opossums, are members of the opossum order, Didelphimorphia.
Nicknamed 'Viking disease,' this hand condition — first surgically treated in 1831 by the surgeon it's named after — permanently curls the ring finger inward. What is it?
Dupuytren's contracture: Medical condition featuring permanent bending of fingers.
A Swedish scientist and inventor until, at 53, dreams and visions sent him into a spiritual phase, this polymath became best known for his 1758 book on the afterlife, Heaven and Hell — who was he?
Emanuel Swedenborg: Swedish scientist, philosopher, and theologian (1688–1772)
With a sweet smell like pear drops, this colorless solvent turns up in nail-polish remover and is used to decaffeinate tea and coffee. What is it?
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit measures a material's ability to store electrical charge, equal to one coulomb per volt — what is it?
Farad: SI unit of electric capacitance.
Patented in 1962 and sold under a brand name synonymous with 'roofies,' this benzodiazepine is notoriously linked to date-rape drug use — what is it?
Flunitrazepam: Benzodiazepine sedative. Flunitrazepam, sold under the brand name Rohypnol among others, is a benzodiazepine used to treat severe insomnia and assist with anesthesia.
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)

This Italian friar and cosmological theorist proposed that stars were distant suns with their own planets, and was tried for heresy by the Roman Inquisition for insisting the universe is infinite — who was he?
Giordano Bruno: Italian Dominican friar, philosopher and mathematician (1548–1600)
This junctional area between the torso and thigh, where the lower abdominal wall meets the leg, is commonly strained in a familiar sports injury — what is it called?
Groin: Area between the torso and the thigh. In human anatomy, the groin, also known as the inguinal region or iliac region, is the junctional area between the torso and the thigh.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, sipping blood, and can neither fly nor jump — its short stumpy legs can't even walk well on a flat surface. What tiny freeloader is it?
Head louse: Insect parasite of humans.
Also called urticaria, this skin condition brings red or flesh-colored raised, itchy bumps that may sting and often follow an allergic reaction — what is it?
Hives: Skin disease characterized by red, raised, and itchy bumps.
Named from Greek words meaning "over" and "formation," this condition enlarges tissue by increasing the number of cells rather than their size — which term, distinct from hypertrophy?
Hyperplasia: Enlargement of tissue due to cell proliferation.
Commonly known as chaga, this parasitic fungus grows on birch trees and forms a charcoal-like black mass often marketed, questionably, as a health supplement — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus: Species of fungus. Inonotus obliquus, commonly called chaga (a Latinization of the Russian word ча́га), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow, this American mathematician's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual resolution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who was she?

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'hump,' this abnormal, excessive curving of the upper spine can result from osteoporosis, disc disease, or a condition common in teens called Scheuermann's disease — what is it called?
Kyphosis: Excessive convex curvature of the lower and middle spine.
Used to treat everything from pneumonia to Legionnaires' disease, this broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic is the left-handed mirror-image isomer of a drug called ofloxacin — what is it?
Levofloxacin: Antibiotic. Levofloxacin, sold under the brand name Levaquin among others, is a broad-spectrum antibiotic of the fluoroquinolone drug class.
Patented in 1980 and marketed as Claritin, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever and hives but can still cause sleepiness and dry mouth — what is it?
Loratadine: Antihistamine medication. Loratadine, sold under the brand name Claritin among others, is a medication used to treat allergies.
Genetically related to the Bichon, Bolognese, and Havanese, this toy breed sports a silky white coat, doesn't shed, and tops out around 4 kilograms — what breed is it?
Maltese dog: Breed of toy dog. The precise link, if any, between the modern and ancient breeds is not known.

Entering US Navy service in 1961 before the Marines and Air Force adopted it too, this twin-engine supersonic jet became America's most-produced supersonic military aircraft with 5,195 built — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II: Fighter aircraft family developed from 1958.
Sold as Flagyl, this antibiotic and antiprotozoal fights everything from giardiasis to trichomoniasis — but it's notorious for leaving a metallic taste in your mouth — what is it?
Metronidazole: Antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication. Metronidazole, sold under the brand name Flagyl and Metrogyl among others, is an antibiotic and antiprotozoal medication.
Making up about 23% of all named marine organisms, this phylum is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after the arthropods — what is it?
This condition describes an abnormally dilated pupil that remains enlarged even in bright light, often triggered by trauma, disease, or certain drugs — what is it called?
Mydriasis: Excessive dilation of the pupil.

This silvery-white transition metal with a faint golden tinge resists corrosion thanks to a thin oxide layer, and in pure native form it's mostly found inside iron meteorites — which element, atomic number 28, is it?
Nickel: Chemical element with atomic number 28 (Ni)
This soft-bodied mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through tiny gaps and propels itself backward by jetting water through a siphon — what eight-limbed creature is it?
Octopus: Soft-bodied eight-limbed order of molluscs.
Sold under the brand name Anavar, this synthetic anabolic steroid helps burn victims and Turner syndrome patients gain weight — what is it?
Oxandrolone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It was sold under the brand names Oxandrin and Anavar, among others.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Despite the naming confusion with true yams, this starchy tuberous root actually belongs to the morning glory family and hails from tropical Ecuador — which crop?
Sweet potato: Species of edible plant.
Famously nicknamed 'white ants,' these wood-munching eusocial insects are actually genetically closer to cockroaches than they are to true ants — what are they?
Termite: Social insects related to cockroaches.
He joined Apple in 1998 to run worldwide operations and stepped up to the top job in 2011 when Steve Jobs resigned — which executive now leads the company?
Estimated to date back to the end of the Jurassic period roughly 156 million years ago, this fungal genus includes several species of truffles prized as culinary delicacies — which genus?
Tuber (fungus): Genus of fungi. Tuber is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).
The primary flavor compound in the vanilla bean, this phenolic aldehyde is now more often made synthetically than extracted from the real pod — what is it?
Vanillin: Chemical compound. Vanillin is an organic compound with the molecular formula C8H8O3.
Native to the Baltic, Black, and Caspian Sea basins, this large freshwater fish's range now stretches from the UK to western China — which species?
Wels catfish: Species of fish. It has been introduced to several countries in Western Europe, Mediterranean and Asia as a prized sport fish.
Following her husband's death, this Russian economist and activist vowed to carry on his opposition work and now chairs the Human Rights Foundation — who is she?
Yulia Navalnaya: Russian economist and political activist (born 1976)
What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
The symbol for oxygen is O. Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
The symbol for terbium is Tb. Terbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tb and atomic number 65.

In what year was Kirk Douglas born?
Kirk Douglas (born Issur Danielovitch; December 9, 1916 – February 5, 2020) was an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Kirstie Alley born?
Kirstie Alley: Kirstie Louise Alley (January 12, 1951 – December 5, 2022) was an American actress.
In what year was Samuel L. Jackson born?
Samuel L. Jackson: Samuel Leroy Jackson (born December 21, 1948) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Guy Ritchie born?
Guy Ritchie: Guy Stuart Ritchie (born 10 September 1968) is an English filmmaker known primarily for British comedy gangster films and large-scale action-adventure films.

In what year was Bryan Cranston born?
